narrative.intro: Axiom Space has $213M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date, across 7 awards with an average award size of $30.4M, and obligations are up 62.7% year over year. The National Aeronautics and Space Administration is the primary buyer, accounting for $213M in obligations. Obligations by fiscal year show a multi-year increase from $1.7M in FY21 to $213M in FY26. Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing is the dominant NAICS market with $211M in obligations, while Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) accounts for $1.7M. The Department of Defense appears as a buyer with $500 in obligations. Current-year totals are partial and reflect fiscal year to date activity. This picture shows concentrated federal demand tied primarily to space manufacturing and R&D activity, with most obligations recorded under NASA and a small amount under DoD.

sections.heading: Who are Axiom Space's largest federal buyers?
sections.body: National Aeronautics and Space Administration obligated $213M to Axiom Space in FY2026 to date. Department of Defense obligated $500 to Axiom Space in FY2026 to date. The buying profile is heavily weighted to NASA, with only a small DoD presence in the provided figures.

sections.heading: What markets does Axiom Space serve for the federal government?
sections.body: Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing is $211M of Axiom Space's federal obligations in FY2026 to date. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) is $1.7M of Axiom Space's federal obligations in FY2026 to date. The company’s federal work is concentrated in space manufacturing and related R&D.

Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing accounts for $211M, and Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) accounts for $1.7M in FY2026 to date.
